#### Setup

```{r setup, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Locate the project root so every subsequent file.path() call is anchored to
# the repo directory regardless of where the qmd is opened or rendered.
# The cascade is: CFMD_BENCH_WORKDIR env var → knitr root.dir → walk up the
# directory tree looking for config.yaml → fall back to getwd().
# The env var override is useful when rendering headlessly (e.g. CI).
find_project_root <- function() {
  env_root <- Sys.getenv("CFMD_BENCH_WORKDIR", unset = "")
  if (nzchar(env_root) && dir.exists(env_root)) return(normalizePath(env_root))

  knitr_root <- tryCatch(
    normalizePath(knitr::opts_knit$get("root.dir"), mustWork = FALSE),
    error = function(e) ""
  )
  if (nzchar(knitr_root) && dir.exists(knitr_root)) return(knitr_root)

  # Walk up from the qmd file location until we find config.yaml (max 10 levels).
  start <- tryCatch(
    dirname(normalizePath(knitr::current_input(), mustWork = FALSE)),
    error = function(e) getwd()
  )
  d <- start
  for (i in seq_len(10L)) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(d, "config.yaml"))) return(d)
    parent <- dirname(d)
    if (parent == d) break
    d <- parent
  }
  getwd()
}

root <- find_project_root()
setwd(root)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
```

#### Methods and Libraries

```{r libraries, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

# cfmdbench_config_helpers.R provides:
#   cfmdbench_load_config()      — reads config.yaml, merges with built-in defaults
#   cfmdbench_resolve_methods()  — validates method IDs from methods$pick
#   cfmdbench_setup_backends()   — configures TabPFN (reticulate) or MLP (torch)
#   %||%                         — null-coalescing operator used throughout
source(file.path(root, "R", "cfmdbench_config_helpers.R"))

# Load and merge config.yaml with built-in defaults.
# If config.yaml is absent, all defaults from cfmdbench_default_config() are used.
cfg <- cfmdbench_load_config(file.path(root, "config.yaml"))

# Expand methods$pick ("all" or a subset like c("ranger", "xgboost")) into a
# named character vector, e.g. c(ranger = "Random Forest", xgboost = "XGBoost").
# This vector is used everywhere: to build learners, to label plots/tables,
# and to gate optional backends.
methods         <- cfmdbench_resolve_methods(cfg$methods$pick)
needs_mlr3torch <- "mlp"    %in% names(methods)
needs_tabpfn    <- "tabpfn" %in% names(methods)

cat("Methods selected:\n"); print(methods)

# ── Package loading ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!requireNamespace("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pacman")

base_pkgs <- c(
  "callr", "coin", "compositions", "conflicted", "cowplot", "data.table", "emoa",
  "factoextra", "FactoMineR", "farff", "fastVoteR", "FSelectorRcpp", "future",
  "future.apply", "httr", "iml", "jsonlite", "kknn", "magrittr",
  "mlr3filters", "mlr3fselect", "mlr3hyperband", "mlr3learners", "mlr3oml",
  "mlr3pipelines", "mlr3tuning", "mlr3tuningspaces", "mlr3viz", "paradox",
  "parallel", "patchwork", "plotly", "progressr", "ranger", "Rtsne", "scales",
  "smotefamily", "stabm", "tidyverse", "vegan", "wordcloud", "wordcloud2",
  "yaml", "zCompositions"
)
# Only load torch/reticulate when the corresponding method is actually selected,
# to avoid triggering the torch download prompt or the conda env check.
torch_pkgs  <- if (needs_mlr3torch) "mlr3torch"  else character()
tabpfn_pkgs <- if (needs_tabpfn)    "reticulate" else character()

# mlr3extralearners is only on GitHub (not CRAN), so it must be installed
# separately before pacman::p_load tries to resolve it.
if (!requireNamespace("remotes",          quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")
if (!requireNamespace("mlr3extralearners", quietly = TRUE))
  remotes::install_github("mlr-org/mlr3extralearners@*release",
                           upgrade = "never", dependencies = TRUE)

pkgs <- unique(c(base_pkgs, torch_pkgs, tabpfn_pkgs))
do.call(pacman::p_load, c(as.list(pkgs), install = TRUE))

# Resolve name collisions between mlr3/tidyverse/compositions that all export
# common generic names. Without this, R would use whichever was loaded last,
# which can change silently between sessions.
conflict_prefer("select",   "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("filter",   "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("rename",   "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("mutate",   "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("first",    "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("var",      "compositions")
conflict_prefer("progress", "httr")

# Load the three helper scripts that define all cfmdbench_* functions.
# These must be sourced AFTER packages are loaded (they depend on mlr3, dplyr, etc.).
source(file.path(root, "R", "cfmdbench_data_helpers.R"))      # download + prepare data
source(file.path(root, "R", "cfmdbench_training_helpers.R"))  # build learners + train
source(file.path(root, "R", "cfmdbench_scoring_helpers.R"))   # benchmark + predict utilities

# Configure optional backends after packages are loaded:
#   TabPFN: sets HF_TOKEN, PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF, activates the conda env
#           (name from TABPFN_ENV_NAME, default "cfmdbench-tabpfn-gpu").
#   MLP:    installs R torch if needed; warns if CUDA is not available.
# TabPFN and MLP are mutually exclusive (both try to initialise a CUDA context).
cfmdbench_setup_backends(cfg, needs_tabpfn, needs_mlr3torch, root)
```

#### Set Parameters

```{r parameters, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Silence mlr3 and bbotk info-level messages during tuning.
# These would otherwise flood the output with per-iteration status lines.
lgr::get_logger("mlr3")$set_threshold("off")
lgr::get_logger("bbotk")$set_threshold("off")

# ── Execution settings (config.yaml → execution section) ──────────────────────
seed         <- cfg$execution$seed        # global random seed for reproducibility
kfold        <- cfg$execution$kfold       # outer CV folds (default 10)
repeats      <- cfg$execution$repeats     # repetitions for repeated CV on small data
num_threads  <- cfg$execution$num_threads %||% parallel::detectCores()
num_jobs     <- kfold   # number of parallel future workers = one per CV fold
term_min     <- cfg$execution$term_min    # tuning time budget per method (minutes)
fast_tuning  <- cfg$execution$fast_tuning # TRUE = budget-based multi-fidelity tuning
learner_fallback <- cfg$execution$learner_fallback  # TRUE = featureless fallback on error

set.seed(seed)
# Raise the future globals size limit to handle large objects (e.g. the full
# dataset, preprocessing pipeline) crossing process boundaries during parallel CV.
options(future.globals.maxSize = cfg$execution$future_globals_max_size_gb * 1024^3)
handlers(global = TRUE)   # enable progressr progress bars globally

# ── Dataset settings (config.yaml → dataset section) ──────────────────────────
ds     <- cfg$dataset$id       # dataset identifier used in file names
ver    <- cfg$dataset$version  # dataset version; also used as the GitHub ref for download
target <- cfg$dataset$target   # column name of the outcome variable (default "category")

# run_date identifies this analysis run; used in save_dir below.
# If left blank in config.yaml it defaults to today's date.
run_date <- cfg$dataset$run_date %||% ""
if (!nzchar(run_date)) run_date <- as.character(Sys.Date())

# save_dir stores all tuned models and tuning instances for this run.
# Format: <date>_<dataset>_<version>_saved_learners/
# A new directory is created if it does not exist; an existing one is reused
# (allowing interrupted runs to be resumed without re-tuning finished methods).
save_dir <- paste(run_date, ds, ver, "saved_learners", sep = "_")
if (!dir.exists(save_dir)) {
  dir.create(save_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  message("Created: ", save_dir)
} else {
  message("Using:   ", save_dir)
}

# ── Data source settings (config.yaml → data_source section) ──────────────────
# cache_dir holds the downloaded TSV files; named by version to keep runs apart.
# manifest_path records the GitHub SHA of each downloaded file so only changed
# files are re-fetched on subsequent runs (SHA-based caching).
cache_dir     <- file.path("cache_cFMD", ver)
manifest_path <- file.path(cache_dir, paste0(ds, "_", ver, "_manifest.rds"))

completeness_threshold <- cfg$data_source$completeness_threshold  # min taxa sum per sample (%)
api_batch_size         <- cfg$data_source$api_batch_size          # GitHub API batch size

# ── Preprocessing settings (config.yaml → preprocessing section) ──────────────
min_samples_per_class <- cfg$preprocessing$min_samples_per_class  # drop rare classes
samples_to_keep       <- cfg$preprocessing$samples_to_keep        # per-class subsampling (1 = keep all)
smote                 <- cfg$preprocessing$smote    # "smote", "blsmote", "adasyn", or "" (auto)
filtering             <- cfg$preprocessing$filtering  # "minimal", "varcor", "infogain"
selecting             <- cfg$preprocessing$selecting  # TRUE = run recursive feature selection

# ── Visualisation settings (config.yaml → visualisation section) ──────────────
downsample_n    <- cfg$visualisation$downsample_n    # max samples for ordination plots
prevalence_min  <- cfg$visualisation$prevalence_min  # min feature prevalence for ordination
shap_n_samples  <- cfg$visualisation$shap_n_samples  # background dataset size for SHAP
shap_n_features <- cfg$visualisation$shap_n_features # number of top features to show in SHAP plots
```

#### Import Data

```{r import, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# cfmdbench_load_data() is the single entry point for all data fetching.
# It calls the GitHub Contents API to list projects, downloads per-project
# TSV files (with SHA-based caching — only changed files are re-fetched),
# parses them with cfmdbench_parse_profile_tsv(), and assembles a tidy
# sample × feature tibble via cfmdbench_prepare_data().
#
# Key config values used:
#   cfg$data_source$repo  — GitHub repo slug (e.g. "SegataLab/cFMD")
#   cfg$data_source$path  — sub-path inside the repo containing project folders
#   ver (= cfg$dataset$version)  — Git ref / tag pinned for reproducibility
#   completeness_threshold — drop samples whose taxa abundances sum < this %
#   api_batch_size         — projects fetched per GitHub API round (rate limiting)
#
# Returns: a tibble with columns for each taxon (k__... prefix) and metadata
# fields (category, type, subtype, sample). This is the raw, unfiltered table.
tab_raw <- cfmdbench_load_data(
  repo                   = cfg$data_source$repo,
  data_path              = cfg$data_source$path,
  ref                    = ver,
  cache_dir              = cache_dir,
  manifest_path          = manifest_path,
  completeness_threshold = completeness_threshold,
  batch_size             = api_batch_size
)

# Quality check: flag samples whose relative abundances don't sum to ~100%.
# These can arise from poor sequencing depth or data export artefacts.
# The plot helps decide whether to tighten completeness_threshold.
sample_cols     <- grep("^k__", names(tab_raw), value = TRUE)
taxa_wide       <- tab_raw[, sample_cols]
col_sums_all    <- colSums(
  suppressWarnings(apply(taxa_wide, 2L, as.numeric)), na.rm = TRUE)
bad_samples     <- names(col_sums_all)[abs(col_sums_all - 100) > 1e-3]

if (length(bad_samples)) {
  bad_df <- data.frame(
    sample  = bad_samples,
    Sum     = as.numeric(col_sums_all[bad_samples]),
    Project = sapply(strsplit(bad_samples, "__"), `[`, 1L)
  )
  p <- ggplot(bad_df, aes(x = Sum, y = reorder(sample, Sum),
                           text = paste("Project:", Project))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
    facet_wrap(~ Project, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "Sum", y = "Sample") +
    theme_minimal()
  ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
} else {
  message("All samples pass the completeness check (sum ~ 100).")
}
```

#### Pre-Process I

```{r preprocess1, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Convert taxa columns to numeric, cast the target to factor, and restrict to
# the three column types that downstream code expects: sample ID, target, and
# taxa (k__...). Metadata columns (type, subtype, etc.) are dropped here.
tab <- tab_raw %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("k__"), as.numeric)) %>%
  mutate(
    !!as.symbol(target) := factor(
      !!as.symbol(target),
      levels = sort(unique(!!as.symbol(target)))
    )
  ) %>%
  select(sample, !!as.symbol(target), starts_with("k__"))

# Rename the target column to the generic name "target" so mlr3 task creation
# is consistent regardless of what the column is called in config.yaml.
names(tab)[names(tab) == target] <- "target"

# Filter out rare classes (< min_samples_per_class from preprocessing$min_samples_per_class)
# and optionally subsample each class to samples_to_keep fraction
# (from preprocessing$samples_to_keep; 1 = keep all samples).
# droplevels() removes empty factor levels left by the filter so mlr3 doesn't
# see ghost classes with zero samples.
tab <- tab %>%
  group_by(target) %>%
  mutate(n = n()) %>%
  filter(n >= min_samples_per_class) %>%
  slice_sample(prop = samples_to_keep) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-n) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  droplevels()

# Determine classification type (binary or multi-class) and set the
# corresponding evaluation metrics used throughout the notebook:
#   dataset_attr    — "binary" or "multi-class"; controls XGBoost eval metrics
#                     and which benchmark measures are computed.
#   bmr_measures    — full metric set for the outer benchmark (reported in tables).
#   train_measures  — inner CV metrics used during tuning (bacc + logloss for both).
#   positive_class  — for binary tasks, the minority class is treated as positive
#                     (relevant for precision, recall, AUC, PR-AUC).
positive_class <- ""
if (length(levels(tab$target)) > 2L) {
  dataset_attr  <- "multi-class"
  bmr_measures  <- c("classif.acc", "classif.bacc", "classif.logloss")
  train_measures <- c("classif.bacc", "classif.logloss")
} else if (length(levels(tab$target)) == 2L) {
  dataset_attr  <- "binary"
  bmr_measures  <- c("classif.acc", "classif.bacc", "classif.logloss",
                     "classif.precision", "classif.recall", "classif.specificity",
                     "classif.fbeta", "classif.auc", "classif.prauc")
  train_measures <- c("classif.bacc", "classif.logloss")
  if (!nzchar(positive_class)) {
    positive_class <- names(which.min(table(tab$target)))
  }
} else {
  stop("Target column has < 2 classes — check the data or the target setting.")
}

cat("\nClassification type:", dataset_attr, "\n")
cat("Evaluation metrics: ", paste(train_measures, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Replace pipe characters in column names (QIIME-style lineages use "|" as
# separator) with underscores, which are safe in mlr3 column names.
tab %<>% rename_with(~ gsub("\\|", "_", .))
tab %<>% sample_frac(size = 1)  # shuffle row order before splitting
```

#### Visualize Data II

```{r visualize2, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Ordination helper: CLR-transforms the abundance matrix, applies optional
# downsampling (downsample_n from visualisation$downsample_n), and filters
# features by prevalence (prevalence_min from visualisation$prevalence_min).
# CLR (centred log-ratio) is the standard transformation for compositional data
# because it maps from the simplex to Euclidean space, making PCA/t-SNE valid.
.make_ordination_df <- function(tab_in, downsample_n, prevalence_min) {
  df        <- as_tibble(tab_in) %>% mutate(target = str_replace_all(target, "_", " "))
  taxa_cols <- setdiff(names(df), c("target", "sample"))

  # Shorten taxon names to species or genus level for readable plot labels.
  shorten_one <- function(n) {
    if (grepl("s__", n)) return(sub(".*(s__.*)$", "\\1", n))
    if (grepl("g__", n)) return(sub(".*(g__.*)$", "\\1", n))
    n
  }
  new_names <- make.unique(vapply(taxa_cols, shorten_one, character(1L)), sep = "_")
  names(df)[match(taxa_cols, names(df))] <- new_names

  y <- df$target
  X <- df[, !(names(df) %in% c("target", "sample")), drop = FALSE]

  # Subsample for speed: PCA/t-SNE on thousands of samples is slow.
  if (nrow(X) > downsample_n) {
    idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(X)), downsample_n)
    X <- X[idx, , drop = FALSE]; y <- y[idx]
  }

  # Remove features present in fewer than prevalence_min fraction of samples
  # (rare taxa add noise to ordination without contributing signal), and remove
  # zero-variance features (these would cause CLR to produce NaN).
  prev <- colMeans(X > 0)
  X    <- X[, prev >= prevalence_min,    drop = FALSE]
  X    <- X[, apply(X, 2L, var) > 0,    drop = FALSE]
  if (!ncol(X)) stop("All features filtered; lower prevalence_min.")

  # Replace zero counts with small imputed values (CZM = count zero multiplicative)
  # before CLR. Zero counts are undefined under log-transformation.
  X0    <- zCompositions::cmultRepl(as.matrix(X), label = 0, method = "CZM",
                                    z.warning = 1, z.delete = FALSE)
  X_clr <- compositions::clr(X0)
  list(X = X, X_clr = X_clr, y = y)
}

ord <- .make_ordination_df(tab, downsample_n, prevalence_min)

# PCA on CLR-transformed abundances
pca    <- prcomp(ord$X_clr, scale. = TRUE)
scores <- data.frame(PC1 = pca$x[, 1L], PC2 = pca$x[, 2L], target = ord$y)

fviz_eig(pca, addlabels = TRUE)

ggplot(scores, aes(PC1, PC2, fill = target)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white", stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "PCA on CLR-transformed abundances",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", round(100 * summary(pca)$importance[2L, 1L], 1L), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(100 * summary(pca)$importance[2L, 2L], 1L), "%)"))

fviz_contrib(pca, choice = "var", axes = 1:2, top = 10L)

# Elbow plot: find the number of components that explain 90% of variance.
cum_var      <- cumsum(pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2))
n_comp_90    <- which(cum_var >= 0.9)[1L]
cat("Components explaining 90% variance:", n_comp_90, "\n")

ggplot(data.frame(k = seq_along(cum_var), v = cum_var), aes(k, v)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = n_comp_90, color = "dodgerblue3", linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(cum_var)) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Elbow plot of PCA components",
       subtitle = "Reference line: 90% variance threshold",
       x = "Number of components", y = "Cumulative proportion of variance")

# t-SNE on CLR-transformed abundances for non-linear structure.
# Perplexity is capped at 30 and also bounded by (n-1)/3 to satisfy the
# t-SNE requirement that perplexity < n/3.
perplexity <- pmin(30L, floor((nrow(ord$X_clr) - 1L) / 3L))
ts <- Rtsne::Rtsne(ord$X_clr, pca = TRUE, check_duplicates = FALSE,
                   perplexity = perplexity, theta = 0.5, num_threads = 8L)
ts_df <- data.frame(tSNE1 = ts$Y[, 1L], tSNE2 = ts$Y[, 2L], target = ord$y)

ggplot(ts_df, aes(tSNE1, tSNE2, fill = target)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white", stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "t-SNE on CLR-transformed abundances") +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 18), legend.text = element_text(size = 12))
```

#### Define Task

```{r task, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Build the mlr3 classification task from the preprocessed table.
# mlr3 requires a primary key column that uniquely identifies each row.
# We handle the edge case where sample IDs are duplicated across projects by
# creating a unique sample_id column in that situation.
tab$sample <- trimws(as.character(tab$sample))
stopifnot("sample" %in% names(tab), "target" %in% names(tab))

if (anyDuplicated(tab$sample)) {
  dups <- tab$sample[duplicated(tab$sample)]
  message("Duplicated sample IDs: ", length(dups))
  tab$sample_id <- make.unique(tab$sample)
  id_col <- "sample_id"
} else {
  id_col <- "sample"
}

# as_data_backend with an integer primary key avoids mlr3 reordering the rows.
backend  <- mlr3::as_data_backend(tab, primary_key = seq_len(nrow(tab)))
task     <- mlr3::as_task_classif(backend, target = "target")
# Remove sample from the feature set so it is not used as a predictor.
task$set_col_roles("sample", roles = character())

# Stratified 80/20 split: stratification ensures each class is proportionally
# represented in both train and test sets. task_train is used for all tuning
# and benchmarking; task_test is the held-out evaluation set.
split      <- mlr3::partition(task, ratio = 0.8)
task_train <- task$clone(deep = TRUE)$filter(split$train)
task_test  <- task$clone(deep = TRUE)$filter(split$test)

# For binary tasks, set the positive class (the minority class by default).
# This determines which class is used as "positive" for precision, recall,
# and AUC calculations.
if (dataset_attr == "binary") {
  task$positive       <- positive_class
  task_train$positive <- positive_class
  task_test$positive  <- positive_class
}

# Add "stratum" role to target so mlr3 stratifies all resampling operations
# (tuning, benchmark CV) by class, preserving class ratios in each fold.
task$set_col_roles("target",       c("target", "stratum"))
task_train$set_col_roles("target", c("target", "stratum"))
task_test$set_col_roles("target",  c("target", "stratum"))
```

#### Pre-Process II

```{r preprocess2, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Compute class distribution statistics to guide the SMOTE decision.
class_counts    <- table(task_train$data()$target)
majority_class  <- names(which.max(class_counts))
minority_class  <- names(which.min(class_counts))
imbalance_ratio <- class_counts[majority_class] / class_counts[minority_class]

cat("\nClass distribution:\n"); print(class_counts)
cat("Imbalance ratio:", round(imbalance_ratio, 2L), ":1\n")

class_counts_df <- as.data.frame(class_counts)
colnames(class_counts_df) <- c("target", "count")

ggplot(class_counts_df, aes(x = reorder(target, count, decreasing = TRUE),
                              y = count, fill = target)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = count), vjust = -0.5, size = 5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(title = "Class Distribution", x = "Target Class", y = "Count") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# ── SMOTE decision ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Apply oversampling if the imbalance ratio exceeds 1.5:1 AND all classes have
# enough samples. The threshold is fixed here (not in config) because it reflects
# a general best practice rather than a dataset-specific choice.
# cfg$preprocessing$smote can force a specific method or leave it on "auto" ("").
imbalance_threshold <- 1.5
apply_smote <- imbalance_ratio > imbalance_threshold &&
               all(class_counts >= min_samples_per_class)

if (!nzchar(smote)) smote <- if (apply_smote) "smote" else "none"
if (!apply_smote)   smote <- "none"
cat("SMOTE decision:", smote, "\n")

# ── Preprocessing pipeline ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The pipeline is built as a sequence of PipeOps connected with %>>%.
# It is assembled here but NOT trained yet — training happens inside each
# learner's cross-validation folds to avoid data leakage.
#
# "filtering" (cfg$preprocessing$filtering) controls which feature filters are applied:
#   "varcor"    — remove near-zero variance features, then correlated features (Spearman)
#   "minimal" / TRUE / selecting=TRUE — only robustify (impute NAs, fix factor levels) + scale
#   "infogain"  — information-gain based feature filter (tuned fraction in search space)
#   anything else — no preprocessing (just a passthrough nop)
#
# All pipelines except "nop" end with po("scale") to centre and standardise
# features. This is important for distance-based methods (SVM, kNN, LDA).
#
# When selecting=TRUE (recursive feature selection), filtering is forced to
# "minimal" because RFE already performs implicit feature selection — adding a
# variance/correlation filter on top would be redundant and could remove
# features before RFE can evaluate their importance.
if (selecting) filtering <- "minimal"

preprocessing_pipe <- if (filtering == "varcor") {
  mlr3pipelines::ppl("robustify") %>>%
    mlr3pipelines::po("filter", filter = mlr3filters::flt("variance"),
                      id = "variance_filter") %>>%
    mlr3pipelines::po("filter", filter = mlr3filters::flt("find_correlation"),
                      method = "spearman", id = "correlation_filter") %>>%
    mlr3pipelines::po("colapply", applicator = as.numeric,
                      affect_columns = mlr3pipelines::selector_type(
                        c("integer", "logical", "numeric")))
} else if (filtering %in% c(TRUE, "minimal") || selecting) {
  mlr3pipelines::ppl("robustify") %>>%
    mlr3pipelines::po("colapply", applicator = as.numeric,
                      affect_columns = mlr3pipelines::selector_type(
                        c("integer", "logical", "numeric")))
} else if (filtering == "infogain") {
  mlr3pipelines::ppl("robustify") %>>%
    mlr3pipelines::po("filter", filter = mlr3filters::flt("information_gain"),
                      id = "infogain_filter") %>>%
    mlr3pipelines::po("colapply", applicator = as.numeric,
                      affect_columns = mlr3pipelines::selector_type(
                        c("integer", "logical", "numeric")))
} else {
  mlr3pipelines::po("nop")
}

if (!isFALSE(filtering)) {
  preprocessing_pipe <- preprocessing_pipe %>>% mlr3pipelines::po("scale", center = TRUE)
}

# Optionally append a SMOTE oversampling step to address class imbalance.
# Three variants are supported: standard SMOTE, Borderline SMOTE, and ADASYN.
# The SMOTE parameters (K, dup_size) are added to the tuning search space below.
smote_pipe <- NULL
if (apply_smote && smote %in% c("smote", "blsmote", "adasyn")) {
  smote_pipe <- switch(smote,
    smote   = mlr3pipelines::po("smote"),
    blsmote = mlr3pipelines::po("blsmote"),
    adasyn  = mlr3pipelines::po("adas"),
    NULL
  )
}
if (!is.null(smote_pipe)) {
  preprocessing_pipe <- preprocessing_pipe %>>% smote_pipe
}

# Safety patch for mlr3torch compatibility: when mlr3torch is loaded it adds
# "lt" (lazy_tensor) to the feature_types of every registered PipeOp, including
# the ones in our preprocessing pipeline. This causes non-MLP learners to fail
# because they don't know how to handle lazy_tensor inputs. We strip it here.
for (po_name in names(preprocessing_pipe$pipeops)) {
  po_obj <- preprocessing_pipe$pipeops[[po_name]]
  priv   <- po_obj$.__enclos_env__$private
  if (!is.null(priv$.feature_types) && "lt" %in% names(priv$.feature_types)) {
    cat("Removing 'lazy_tensor' from:", po_name, "\n")
    priv$.feature_types <- priv$.feature_types[names(priv$.feature_types) != "lt"]
  }
}

cat("\nFinal preprocessing pipeline:\n"); print(preprocessing_pipe)

# ── Preprocessing search space parameters ─────────────────────────────────────
# These are the tunable parts of the preprocessing pipeline. They are merged
# into each learner's search space inside cfmdbench_get_search_space() so that
# filter fractions and SMOTE settings are optimised jointly with model parameters.
preproc_params <- list()
if (filtering == "varcor") {
  preproc_params <- c(preproc_params, list(
    variance_filter.filter.frac    = paradox::p_dbl(0.5, 1, logscale = TRUE),
    correlation_filter.filter.frac = paradox::p_dbl(0.5, 1, logscale = TRUE)
  ))
} else if (filtering == "infogain") {
  preproc_params <- c(preproc_params, list(
    infogain_filter.filter.frac = paradox::p_dbl(0.2, 1.0, logscale = TRUE)
  ))
}
if (!is.null(smote_pipe)) {
  preproc_params <- c(preproc_params, switch(smote,
    smote   = list(smote.K = paradox::p_int(2L, 5L),
                   smote.dup_size = paradox::p_int(1L, 5L)),
    blsmote = list(blsmote.K = paradox::p_int(2L, 5L),
                   blsmote.dup_size = paradox::p_int(1L, 5L),
                   blsmote.C = paradox::p_int(1L, 5L)),
    adasyn  = list(adas.K = paradox::p_int(2L, 5L)),
    list()
  ))
}
```

#### Feature Selection

```{r feature_selection, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Feature selection thresholds from config.yaml → feature_selection section:
#   num_col: if ncol < num_col, target n_features = 2 (too few features to
#            justify a large selection); otherwise n_features = 10.
#   num_row: if nrow > num_row, use "simple" (single-learner RFE, faster);
#            otherwise use "ensemble" (four learners, more robust but slower).
num_col <- cfg$feature_selection$num_col
num_row <- cfg$feature_selection$num_row

# Cache file for the selected feature set. Persisted to save_dir alongside the
# tuned models so that an R session restart does not force a full RFE redo.
# Delete this file (and re-run the chunk) to force a fresh feature selection.
fs_cache_file <- file.path(save_dir, "selected_features.rds")

if (selecting) {

  # ── Robustify tasks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Applied in both the cached and fresh-run paths because task_train / task_test
  # are always rebuilt from scratch after a session restart. The robustify step
  # is fast and deterministic — re-running it is cheap.
  # Note: the training pipeline (preprocess2 chunk) will apply robustify again
  # internally inside each CV fold to avoid data leakage. That is intentional.
  robust_pipe <- mlr3pipelines::ppl("robustify") %>>%
    mlr3pipelines::po("colapply", applicator = as.numeric,
                      affect_columns = mlr3pipelines::selector_type(
                        c("integer", "logical", "numeric")))
  robust_pipe$train(task_train)
  task_train <- robust_pipe$predict(task_train)[[1L]]
  task_test  <- robust_pipe$predict(task_test)[[1L]]

  # ── Resume from cache ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  if (file.exists(fs_cache_file)) {
    selected_feats <- readRDS(fs_cache_file)
    message("Feature selection: loaded ", length(selected_feats),
            " cached features from ", fs_cache_file)
    message("Delete ", fs_cache_file, " and re-run this chunk to redo selection.")

  } else {
    # ── Full RFE run ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Spin up workers only when actually needed — cache hit skips this.
    future::plan(future::sequential)
    future::plan(future::multisession, workers = num_jobs)

    n_features <- if (task_train$ncol < num_col) 2L else 10L
    fs_method  <- if (task_train$nrow > num_row) "simple" else "ensemble"

    # Recursive Feature Elimination: at each step removes the worst 20% of
    # remaining features (feature_fraction = 0.8) until n_features remain.
    rfe     <- mlr3fselect::fs("rfe", n_features = n_features, feature_fraction = 0.8)

    # svm_rfe callback: SVM has no native variable importance, so this callback
    # computes permutation importance externally to guide RFE. This generates
    # the "Computing permutation importance..." messages during selection.
    svm_rfe <- mlr3fselect::clbk("mlr3fselect.svm_rfe")

    # one_se_rule callback: applies the one-standard-error rule to prefer sparser
    # feature sets — i.e. pick the simplest model whose CV score is within one SE
    # of the best. Reduces overfitting to the feature selection data.
    one_se  <- mlr3fselect::clbk("mlr3fselect.one_se_rule")

    # internal_tuning callback for XGBoost: lets XGBoost use early stopping to
    # automatically determine the optimal nrounds during feature selection, rather
    # than fixing it to a single value. Adds nrounds to the internal search space.
    max_nrounds  <- 500L
    internal_ss  <- paradox::ps(nrounds = paradox::p_int(
      upper = max_nrounds,
      aggr  = function(x) as.integer(mean(unlist(x)))
    ))
    xgb_clbk <- mlr3fselect::clbk("mlr3fselect.internal_tuning",
                                    internal_search_space = internal_ss)

    # Four learners used for feature selection — lightweight configurations
    # designed to evaluate feature subsets quickly, not for final prediction.
    fs_rpart   <- mlr3::lrn("classif.rpart")
    fs_ranger  <- mlr3::lrn("classif.ranger",  importance = "permutation")
    fs_svm     <- mlr3::lrn("classif.svm",     type = "C-classification", kernel = "linear")
    fs_xgboost <- mlr3::lrn("classif.xgboost", nrounds = max_nrounds,
                              early_stopping_rounds = 10L)
    mlr3::set_validate(fs_xgboost, 0.2)   # XGBoost needs a validation split for early stopping
    mlr3::set_threads(fs_ranger,  n = ceiling(num_threads / 5L))
    mlr3::set_threads(fs_xgboost, n = ceiling(num_threads / 5L))

    fs_rpart$id   <- "rpart"
    fs_ranger$id  <- "rf"
    fs_svm$id     <- "svm"
    fs_xgboost$id <- "xgboost"

    if (fs_method == "ensemble") {
      # Ensemble feature selection: runs RFE independently with each of the four
      # learners across 50 subsampling repetitions (80% of rows each time) and
      # aggregates the results into a consensus feature ranking.
      # init_resampling = 50 subsampling repeats: produces a stability estimate
      # (Jaccard index) showing how consistently features are selected.
      # The consensus features are chosen by the knee point of the Pareto front
      # (performance vs. number of features) using the "estimated" method.
      efs <- mlr3fselect::ensemble_fselect(
        fselector          = rfe,
        task               = task_train,
        learners           = list(fs_rpart, fs_ranger, fs_svm, fs_xgboost),
        init_resampling    = mlr3::rsmp("subsampling", repeats = 50L, ratio = 0.8),
        inner_resampling   = mlr3::rsmp("cv", folds = 5L),
        inner_measure      = mlr3::msr("classif.ce"),
        measure            = mlr3::msr("classif.bacc"),
        terminator         = mlr3tuning::trm("none"),
        callbacks          = list(
          rpart   = list(one_se),
          rf      = list(one_se),
          svm     = list(one_se, svm_rfe),
          xgboost = list(one_se, xgb_clbk)
        ),
        store_benchmark_result = FALSE
      )

      print(efs); head(efs$result)
      print(autoplot(efs, type = "performance",  theme = theme_minimal(base_size = 14)))
      print(autoplot(efs, type = "n_features",   theme = theme_minimal(base_size = 14)))
      print(autoplot(efs, type = "pareto",       theme = theme_minimal(base_size = 14)))
      print(autoplot(efs, type = "pareto", pareto_front = "estimated",
                     theme = theme_minimal(base_size = 14)) +
            scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") + labs(title = "Estimated Pareto front"))

      # Knee point: the inflection in the performance–complexity trade-off curve
      # where adding more features yields diminishing returns.
      kp <- efs$knee_points(type = "estimated")
      n_feat <- if (is.na(kp$n_features)) {
        message("Estimated knee point NA — using median feature count.")
        median(efs$result$n_features, na.rm = TRUE)
      } else {
        message("Estimated knee point: ", kp$n_features, " features.")
        kp$n_features
      }

      # Stability: how consistently are the same features selected across repeats?
      # A high Jaccard index (close to 1) means the selected set is robust.
      global_stab <- efs$stability("jaccard", global = TRUE)
      message("Global stability (Jaccard): ", global_stab)
      print(efs$stability("jaccard", global = FALSE))
      print(autoplot(efs, type = "stability", theme = theme_minimal(base_size = 14)) +
            scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1"))

      # Consensus feature ranking using average votes (weighted by learner performance).
      consensus_av  <- efs$feature_ranking(method = "av", committee_size = n_feat,
                                            use_weights = TRUE)
      selected_feats <- consensus_av$feature
      print(consensus_av)
    } else {
      # Simple feature selection: single Random Forest with 5-fold CV.
      # Faster than ensemble but less stable for small datasets.
      fsi_obj <- mlr3fselect::fsi(
        task       = task_train,
        learner    = fs_ranger,
        resampling = mlr3::rsmp("cv", folds = 5L),
        measure    = mlr3::msr("classif.bacc"),
        terminator = mlr3tuning::trm("none")
      )
      rfe$optimize(fsi_obj)
      print(data.table::as.data.table(fsi_obj$result)[, .(features, classif.bacc)])
      selected_feats <- fsi_obj$result_feature_set
    }

    # Save selected features to disk so a session restart doesn't require
    # re-running the full RFE. Stored in save_dir alongside tuned models.
    saveRDS(selected_feats, fs_cache_file)
    message("Feature selection: saved ", length(selected_feats),
            " features to ", fs_cache_file)
  }

  # Restrict both tasks to the selected feature subset before training.
  task_train$select(selected_feats)
  task_test$select(selected_feats)
}
```

#### Visualize Data III

```{r visualize3, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Repeat the ordination plots on the post-feature-selection dataset.
# Comparing these with the pre-selection plots shows whether selected features
# preserve the main sources of variation in the data.
if (selecting) {
  ord_post <- .make_ordination_df(task_train$data(), downsample_n, prevalence_min)

  pca_post    <- prcomp(ord_post$X_clr, scale. = TRUE)
  scores_post <- data.frame(PC1 = pca_post$x[, 1L], PC2 = pca_post$x[, 2L],
                             target = ord_post$y)

  print(fviz_eig(pca_post, addlabels = TRUE))

  print(ggplot(scores_post, aes(PC1, PC2, fill = target)) +
    geom_point(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white", stroke = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") + theme_bw() +
    labs(title = "PCA on CLR (post feature selection)",
         x = paste0("PC1 (", round(100 * summary(pca_post)$importance[2L, 1L], 1L), "%)"),
         y = paste0("PC2 (", round(100 * summary(pca_post)$importance[2L, 2L], 1L), "%)")))

  print(fviz_contrib(pca_post, choice = "var", axes = 1:2, top = 10L))

  perp2 <- pmin(30L, floor((nrow(ord_post$X_clr) - 1L) / 3L))
  ts2   <- Rtsne::Rtsne(ord_post$X_clr, pca = TRUE, check_duplicates = FALSE,
                         perplexity = perp2, theta = 0.5, num_threads = 8L)
  ts2_df <- data.frame(tSNE1 = ts2$Y[, 1L], tSNE2 = ts2$Y[, 2L], target = ord_post$y)

  print(ggplot(ts2_df, aes(tSNE1, tSNE2, fill = target)) +
    geom_point(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white", stroke = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") + theme_bw() +
    labs(title = "t-SNE on CLR (post feature selection)") +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 18)))
}
```

#### Train Models

```{r train, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Reset future plan before starting the training parallel loop.
future::plan(future::sequential)
future::plan(future::multisession, workers = num_jobs)

# cfmdbench_build_learners() (R/cfmdbench_training_helpers.R):
#   Creates the base mlr3 Learner objects for all selected methods.
#   No training happens here — these are plain learner specs that get cloned
#   and wrapped in preprocessing pipelines inside cfmdbench_train_methods().
#   Passing methods = names(methods) prevents unnecessary construction of
#   MLP/TabPFN objects when those methods are not selected.
base_learners <- cfmdbench_build_learners(seed = seed, kfold = kfold,
                                           methods = names(methods))

# cfmdbench_train_methods() (R/cfmdbench_training_helpers.R):
#   The main training loop. For each method it:
#     1. Assembles the full pipeline: preprocessing_pipe → learner
#     2. Runs inner-CV tuning using the search space from cfmdbench_get_search_space()
#        with the tuner from cfmdbench_get_tuner() and terminator from
#        cfmdbench_get_terminator()
#     3. Picks the best hyperparameters (highest bacc, then lowest logloss)
#     4. Trains the final model on the full task_train
#     5. Saves <method>_tuned_instance.rds (tuning history) and
#        <method>_tuned_learner.rds (final trained model) to save_dir
#   Methods with an existing completed instance on disk are skipped,
#   allowing interrupted runs to be resumed without re-tuning.
#
# Key config values used by this function:
#   execution$kfold        → inner CV folds
#   execution$repeats      → repeated CV repetitions for small datasets
#   execution$num_threads  → total threads; divided among parallel jobs
#   execution$term_min     → tuning time budget per method (minutes)
#   execution$fast_tuning  → multi-fidelity tuning with budget parameters
#   execution$learner_fallback → featureless fallback on learner error
#
# Returns: named list of trained GraphLearner objects (also on disk in save_dir).
trained_learners <- cfmdbench_train_methods(
  methods           = methods,
  base_learners     = base_learners,
  preprocessing_pipe = preprocessing_pipe,
  preproc_params    = preproc_params,
  task_train        = task_train,
  train_measures    = train_measures,
  dataset_attr      = dataset_attr,
  save_dir          = save_dir,
  kfold             = kfold,
  repeats           = repeats,
  num_threads       = num_threads,
  num_jobs          = num_jobs,
  fast_tuning       = fast_tuning,
  learner_fallback  = learner_fallback,
  term_min          = term_min
)
```

#### Benchmark

```{r benchmark, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# The benchmark chunk re-evaluates every tuned model using k-fold CV on task_train.
# This is separate from the test-set prediction (next chunk) and gives a more
# reliable estimate of generalisation by averaging across multiple train/val splits.
measure <- c(accuracy = "classif.acc")

future::plan(future::sequential)
future::plan(future::multisession, workers = num_jobs)

# Choose benchmark resampling strategy:
#   bootstrap (if the smallest class has <= kfold samples): avoids empty test
#              strata that would crash stratified k-fold CV.
#   cv        (otherwise): standard k-fold is preferred when class sizes allow it.
# The 10 bootstrap repetitions match the kfold default to keep compute comparable.
min_count <- task_train$data() %>%
  dplyr::count(target) %>% dplyr::pull(n) %>% min()

benchmark_resampling <- if (min_count <= kfold) {
  mlr3::rsmp("bootstrap", repeats = 10L, ratio = 1)
} else {
  mlr3::rsmp("cv", folds = kfold)
}

# cfmdbench_load_benchmark_learners() (R/cfmdbench_scoring_helpers.R):
#   Loads each learner from trained_learners (in-memory, preferred) or from
#   <method>_tuned_learner.rds on disk (fallback for methods not in this session).
#   Also: unmarshals MLP models (reverses the tensor→raw-bytes serialisation),
#   sets threads = 1 (benchmark runs learners in parallel at the outer level),
#   and re-trains each learner on task_train to ensure graph state is current.
learners_best <- cfmdbench_load_benchmark_learners(
  methods, trained_learners, save_dir, task_train)

# cfmdbench_get_preproc_summary() (R/cfmdbench_scoring_helpers.R):
#   Inspects the trained pipeline's internal PipeOp outputs to report:
#     - how many features survived preprocessing (after SMOTE / scale)
#     - the class distribution as seen by the learner (post-SMOTE if applied)
#   This requires keep_results = TRUE (set in cfmdbench_configure_final_learner).
#   The `after` argument identifies which PipeOp to inspect: "smote" when
#   SMOTE was applied, "scale" otherwise.
for (method in names(learners_best)) {
  summary <- suppressWarnings(
    cfmdbench_get_preproc_summary(learners_best[[method]],
                                   after = if (apply_smote) smote else "scale"))
  if (!is.null(summary)) {
    cat(sprintf("\n--- [%s] ---\n", method))
    if (!is.na(summary$n_features)) {
      cat(sprintf("Final features (%d):\n", summary$n_features))
      print(summary$features)
      cat("Class distribution:\n"); print(summary$class_distribution)
    } else {
      cat("No Task output; see filter summary above.\n")
    }
  }
}

# Run benchmark: evaluates all learners using the same resampling design so
# results are directly comparable. mlr3::benchmark() runs each learner ×
# each fold in parallel (managed by the future plan set above).
start_bmr <- Sys.time()
cat("Benchmark start:", format(start_bmr, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n")
bmr <- mlr3::benchmark(
  design = mlr3::benchmark_grid(task_train, learners_best, benchmark_resampling))
cat("Benchmark done: ", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n")
cat("Time:", round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start_bmr, units = "mins")), 2),
    "minutes\n")

# Box plot of CV accuracy per method
autoplot(bmr, measure = mlr3::msr(measure[[1L]])) +
  labs(x = "Method", y = paste(names(measure[1L]), "measure")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = as.character(unlist(methods))) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title  = element_text(size = 16),
        plot.title  = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0.5))

# cfmdbench_format_bench_df() (R/cfmdbench_scoring_helpers.R):
#   Converts the mlr3 BenchmarkResult aggregate to a tidy data.frame:
#   drops bookkeeping columns, translates mlr3 metric IDs to human-readable
#   names (e.g. "classif.bacc" → "balanced accuracy"), and rounds to 4 decimal places.
#   bmr_measures is the metric vector set in preprocess1 (differs for binary vs multi-class).
bench_df <- cfmdbench_format_bench_df(bmr, bmr_measures)
print(bench_df %>% select(-learner_id))

# Dodged barplot comparing accuracy, balanced accuracy, and logloss
bench_long <- bench_df %>%
  select(method, accuracy, `balanced accuracy`, logloss) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(accuracy, `balanced accuracy`, logloss),
               names_to = "measure", values_to = "value")

metric_colors <- c(accuracy = "skyblue3", `balanced accuracy` = "dodgerblue3",
                   logloss = "tomato3")

ggplot(bench_long, aes(x = method, y = value, fill = measure)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = metric_colors) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2L)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = 1.5,
            color = "white", size = 3L) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Model performance measures", x = "Method", y = "Value") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title  = element_text(size = 16),
        plot.title  = element_text(size = 18))

# Identify the best model: highest balanced accuracy, then lowest logloss.
# best_model_id is the learner_id (internal GraphLearner ID, e.g. "ranger");
# best_method is the human-readable label (e.g. "Random Forest").
# These are used in the prediction and importance chunks below.
best_row      <- bench_df %>% arrange(desc(`balanced accuracy`), logloss) %>% slice(1L)
best_model_id <- best_row$learner_id
best_method   <- best_row$method

# Average fold-wise predictions for the best model to summarise training-set
# performance. Each sample appears in exactly one test fold per CV run.
pred_dt    <- data.table::as.data.table(bmr$score())
best_preds <- pred_dt[stringr::str_detect(learner_id, best_model_id)]
all_preds  <- best_preds$prediction_test %>%
  purrr::map_dfr(~ data.table::as.data.table(.x) %>% tibble::as_tibble())
prob_cols  <- grep("^prob\\.", names(all_preds), value = TRUE)

if (length(prob_cols) == 2L) {
  # Binary: average the positive-class probability across folds, then threshold.
  positive_col <- paste0("prob.", positive_class)
  avg_preds <- all_preds %>%
    group_by(row_ids) %>%
    summarise(prob_positive = mean(.data[[positive_col]]),
              truth = first(truth), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(
      response = if_else(prob_positive >= 0.5, positive_class,
                         setdiff(levels(truth), positive_class)),
      response = factor(response, levels = levels(truth)),
      correct  = response == truth
    )
} else {
  # Multi-class: take the class with the highest average probability.
  avg_preds <- all_preds %>%
    group_by(row_ids) %>%
    summarise(
      response = names(which.max(colMeans(across(all_of(prob_cols))))),
      truth = first(truth), .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(response = sub("prob\\.", "", response),
           response = factor(response, levels = levels(truth)),
           correct  = response == truth)
}

pred_summary <- avg_preds %>%
  group_by(truth, correct) %>%
  summarise(N = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(truth) %>%
  mutate(prop = N / sum(N)) %>%
  ungroup()

p1 <- ggplot(pred_summary, aes(x = truth, y = N, fill = correct, label = N)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  geom_text(position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "dodgerblue3", "FALSE" = "red3")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Absolute Counts", x = "True Class", y = "Count", fill = "Correct") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1))

p2 <- ggplot(pred_summary,
             aes(x = truth, y = prop, fill = correct,
                 label = sprintf("%.0f%%", prop * 100))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +
  geom_text(position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "dodgerblue3", "FALSE" = "red3")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Proportion Correct", x = "True Class", y = "Proportion", fill = "Correct") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1))

p3 <- ggplot(avg_preds, aes(x = truth, y = response, color = correct)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.4, width = 0.25, height = 0.25) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "dodgerblue3", "FALSE" = "red3")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "True vs Predicted", x = "True Class", y = "Predicted", color = "Correct") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1))

(p1 + p2 + p3) + plot_layout(ncol = 3) +
  plot_annotation(title = paste("Prediction Overview —", best_method),
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold",
                                                          hjust = 0.5)))
```

#### Prediction

```{r prediction, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Evaluate each tuned model on the held-out test set (task_test = 20% of data).
# This is a single prediction per model — no resampling — giving an unbiased
# estimate of generalisation performance on data the model has never seen.
predictions <- list()

for (method in names(methods)) {
  best_model <- learners_best[[method]]

  # Fall back to disk if the model wasn't loaded in the benchmark chunk
  # (e.g. if this chunk is run in a fresh session).
  if (is.null(best_model)) {
    path <- file.path(save_dir, paste0(method, "_tuned_learner.rds"))
    if (!file.exists(path)) {
      cat("SKIP:", method, "— no tuned learner found.\n"); next
    }
    best_model <- readRDS(path)
    try(best_model$unmarshal(), silent = TRUE)  # unmarshal MLP tensors if needed
    best_model$train(task_train)
  }

  pred              <- best_model$predict(task_test)
  predictions[[method]] <- pred
  sc                <- pred$score(mlr3::msr("classif.acc"))
  cat("\nclassif.acc of", methods[[method]], ":", round(sc, 2L), "\n")

  pred_tab       <- data.frame(truth = pred$truth, response = pred$response, pred$prob)
  pred_tab$match <- ifelse(pred_tab$truth == pred_tab$response, "TRUE", "FALSE")
  print(pred_tab %>% count(match) %>% mutate(ratio = round(n / sum(n), 2L)))

  # assign() creates objects named e.g. "ranger_test_predict" and "ranger_pred_df"
  # in this chunk's environment. cfmdbench_gather_pred_tabs() and
  # cfmdbench_gather_pred_performance() (below) discover them automatically via
  # ls(pattern = ...) so we don't need to maintain an explicit list.
  assign(paste(method, "test", "predict", sep = "_"), pred_tab)
  assign(paste(method, "pred", "df",      sep = "_"),
         pred$score(measures = lapply(bmr_measures, mlr3::msr)))
}

# cfmdbench_gather_pred_performance() (R/cfmdbench_scoring_helpers.R):
#   Collects all <method>_pred_df objects from this environment, applies the
#   same column renaming as cfmdbench_format_bench_df(), and optionally
#   restricts to the same columns as bench_df so both tables align for comparison.
pred_df <- cfmdbench_gather_pred_performance(env = environment(), bench_df = bench_df)
print(pred_df)

# cfmdbench_gather_pred_tabs() (R/cfmdbench_scoring_helpers.R):
#   Collects all <method>_test_predict data.frames and binds them into a single
#   long data.frame with a `method` column — convenient for faceted ggplot comparisons.
pred_tabs <- cfmdbench_gather_pred_tabs(env = environment())
plot_df   <- pred_tabs %>%
  mutate(truth = factor(truth, levels = task_test$class_names),
         match = factor(match, levels = c("TRUE", "FALSE"))) %>%
  count(method, truth, match, name = "n") %>%
  group_by(method, truth) %>%
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n), label = paste0(round(pct, 1L), "%")) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = truth, y = pct, fill = match)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            color = "white", size = 3L) +
  facet_grid(method ~ ., scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "dodgerblue3", "FALSE" = "red3"),
                    name = "Correct") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1L),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Class", y = "Percent of predictions",
       title = "Test predictions by class and method") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 18))
```

#### Performance Comparison

```{r performance_comparison, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Dumbbell plots comparing CV benchmark scores (train folds) vs held-out test
# scores. The gap between the two points indicates overfitting: a large gap
# means the model performs well on training data but generalises less well.
metric_cols <- setdiff(names(bench_df), c("method", "learner_id"))

bench_long2 <- bench_df %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(metric_cols), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(dataset = "Train (Benchmark)")

pred_long2 <- pred_df %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(metric_cols), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(dataset = "Test (Prediction)")

dumbbell_df <- bind_rows(bench_long2, pred_long2) %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = rev(sort(unique(metric))))) %>%
  select(method, metric, dataset, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = dataset, values_from = value)

ggplot(dumbbell_df, aes(y = metric, group = method)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = `Train (Benchmark)`, xend = `Test (Prediction)`,
                   y = metric, yend = metric),
               color = "gray60", linewidth = 1.2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(x = `Train (Benchmark)`, color = "Train"), size = 3L) +
  geom_point(aes(x = `Test (Prediction)`,  color = "Test"),  size = 3L) +
  facet_wrap(~ method, ncol = 1L, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Train = "green3", Test = "magenta3")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16L) +
  labs(title = "Model Performance: Train vs Test",
       x = "Score", y = "Metric", color = "Dataset") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "right")

ggplot(dumbbell_df, aes(y = method, group = metric)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = `Train (Benchmark)`, xend = `Test (Prediction)`, yend = method),
               color = "gray60", linewidth = 1.2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(x = `Train (Benchmark)`, color = "Train"), size = 3L) +
  geom_point(aes(x = `Test (Prediction)`,  color = "Test"),  size = 3L) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Train = "green3", Test = "magenta3")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16L) +
  labs(title = "Model Performance: Train vs Test",
       x = "Score", y = "Method", color = "Dataset") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey70", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.6),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(1.2, "lines"),
        legend.position = "right")
```

#### Feature Importance

```{r importance, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# SHAP computation + plots.
# We use best_model_id (set in the benchmark chunk as the learner with highest
# balanced accuracy). shap_n_samples (cfg$visualisation$shap_n_samples,
# default 100) controls how many background samples are used.
method <- best_model_id

# Strip the long NCBI-style lineage prefix (e.g. "k__Bacteria|p__...|s__X_Y")
# down to just the species or strain name for readable plot labels.
parse_taxon_name <- function(name) {
  parsed <- stringr::str_extract(name, "(?<=_s__).*")
  stringr::str_replace_all(parsed, "_t__", "_")
}

temp_dat  <- task_train$data()
temp_tab  <- temp_dat %>% dplyr::select(-target) %>% as.data.frame()
temp_targ <- temp_dat$target

original_names   <- colnames(temp_tab)
simplified_names <- vapply(original_names, parse_taxon_name, FUN.VALUE = character(1L))
name_mapping     <- setNames(simplified_names, original_names)

# Load the model: prefer the in-memory trained_learners list (available when
# this chunk runs in the same session as the train chunk). Fall back to the
# saved RDS file if running in a fresh session.
imodel <- if (!is.null(trained_learners[[method]])) {
  trained_learners[[method]]
} else {
  readRDS(file.path(save_dir, paste0(method, "_tuned_learner.rds")))
}

# iml::Predictor wraps any mlr3 learner into a model-agnostic interface.
# type = "prob" returns class probabilities so SHAP can be computed per class.
temp_pred <- iml::Predictor$new(model = imodel, data = temp_tab,
                                 y = temp_targ, type = "prob")

# MLP and TabPFN are not thread-safe in multisession (Python/torch context
# cannot be forked across workers), so use sequential for those methods.
future::plan(future::sequential)
if (!method %in% c("mlp", "tabpfn"))
  future::plan(future::multisession, workers = num_threads)

# Subsample background dataset to shap_n_samples (cfg$visualisation$shap_n_samples).
# Computing SHAP for every training sample would be prohibitively slow.
n_samp <- min(shap_n_samples, nrow(temp_tab))
idx    <- sample.int(nrow(temp_tab), n_samp)
temp_small <- temp_tab[idx, , drop = FALSE]

# Compute SHAP values for each sampled observation. iml::Shapley computes
# exact Shapley values by marginalising over all feature orderings using the
# background dataset. Each call returns a data.frame with phi (SHAP value)
# per feature per class.
shap_list <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(temp_small)), function(i) {
  s <- iml::Shapley$new(temp_pred, x.interest = temp_small[i, , drop = FALSE])
  dplyr::mutate(s$results, sample_id = idx[i])
})
shap_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(shap_list)

# Aggregate: mean absolute SHAP across samples gives a global feature importance
# score. Higher = more influential for the model's predictions on average.
# shap_n_features (cfg$visualisation$shap_n_features, default 10) controls
# how many top features are shown in the plots.
shap_agg <- shap_all %>%
  dplyr::group_by(feature) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean_abs_phi = mean(abs(phi)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(feature_pretty = dplyr::recode(feature, !!!name_mapping)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(mean_abs_phi)) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = shap_n_features)

# Per-class aggregation used by the directional plot below.
# Positive phi = feature increases P(that class); negative = decreases.
class_contrib <- shap_all %>%
  dplyr::group_by(feature, class) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean_phi = mean(phi), mean_abs_phi = mean(abs(phi)),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(feature_pretty = dplyr::recode(feature, !!!name_mapping),
                class = stringr::str_replace_all(class, "_", " ")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(feature %in% shap_agg$feature)

classes <- sort(unique(class_contrib$class))

if (length(classes) == 2L) {
  # Binary: show SHAP for the reference class (first alphabetically).
  # Positive mean_phi → feature increases P(reference class).
  # Negative mean_phi → feature decreases P(reference class).
  # The direction label is created as a character column so scale_fill_manual
  # can match it by name directly, avoiding the unreliable positional-label
  # behaviour that occurs when fill is a bare logical (TRUE/FALSE).
  ref <- classes[1L]
  ggplot(class_contrib %>%
           dplyr::filter(class == ref) %>%
           dplyr::mutate(direction = ifelse(mean_phi > 0,
                                            "Increases P(ref)",
                                            "Decreases P(ref)")),
         aes(x = reorder(feature_pretty, mean_phi), y = mean_phi,
             fill = direction)) +
    geom_col() + coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Increases P(ref)" = "#1f78b4",
                                 "Decreases P(ref)" = "#e31a1c")) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(title = paste("Class-specific SHAP (reference:", ref, ")"),
         subtitle = paste(n_samp, "samples,", shap_n_features, "features"),
         x = "Feature", y = paste("Mean SHAP for", ref), fill = "Effect") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 18))
} else {
  # Multi-class: one facet panel per class, fill by direction.
  # Dodging many classes in a single panel is unreadable; faceting keeps each
  # class legible and uses the same blue/red direction convention as the binary
  # plot above (blue = increases P(class), red = decreases P(class)).
  ggplot(class_contrib %>%
           dplyr::mutate(direction = ifelse(mean_phi > 0,
                                            "Increases P(class)",
                                            "Decreases P(class)")),
         aes(x = reorder(feature_pretty, mean_abs_phi),
             y = mean_phi, fill = direction)) +
    geom_col() + coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Increases P(class)" = "#1f78b4",
                                 "Decreases P(class)" = "#e31a1c")) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
    facet_wrap(~ class, scales = "free_x") +
    labs(title = "Class-specific SHAP contributions",
         subtitle = paste(n_samp, "samples,", shap_n_features, "features"),
         x = "Feature (taxon)", y = "Mean SHAP value", fill = "Effect") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 12),
          axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10),
          axis.title   = element_text(size = 14),
          plot.title   = element_text(size = 18),
          strip.text   = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
          legend.position = "bottom")
}
```
